coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For A Mind
That Won't Sit Still
coverDek: For the racing thoughts at 2am, the what-ifs that won't quit, and the peace that actually outlasts them.

points.hook: Lord, my mind is a courtroom and I am both the prosecutor and the accused.
paragraphs: Father, I'm tired of cross-examining my own life at midnight — replaying conversations, rehearsing disasters that haven't happened, building a case against a future You haven't even written yet. I lay the gavel down. You are the Judge here, not me, and Your verdict over my life is already mercy. Quiet the courtroom in my head tonight.
points.verseText: “Be careful for nothing; but in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God, which passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus.”

points.hook: Let me tell you what anxiety actually is: worship pointed at the wrong throne.
paragraphs: Every fear is just faith aimed in the wrong direction — full confidence that the worst is coming. So today I'm not asking you to stop feeling. I'm asking you to redirect the energy. Take the same intensity you've been giving your what-ifs and hand it to the God who already has what-is covered. Cast the whole care — not manage it, not medicate it into silence — cast it, like you're throwing something heavy off your own back onto shoulders strong enough to hold it.
points.verseText: “Casting all your care upon him; for he careth for you.”

points.hook: Your body has been keeping score of every thought you haven't brought to Me.
paragraphs: I know the tight chest, the shallow breath, the sleep that won't come. I made you with a nervous system that reacts to threat — and I'm not asking you to override your biology with a Bible verse and pretend the clenched jaw isn't real. I'm asking you to let Me into the room where the fear lives, not just the room where you perform having it together. Bring Me the body, not just the testimony.
points.verseText: “The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want... he leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul.”

points.hook: Anxiety loves to isolate you — it convinces you that carrying it alone is safer than being seen with it.
paragraphs: Here's the trick it plays: it tells you nobody would understand, so you go quiet, and the silence makes the thought louder, and the louder thought makes you quieter still. Break that cycle today. Say the fear out loud to God, then say it out loud to one person who loves you. A burden named out loud has already lost half its weight — you just haven't felt the difference yet.
points.verseText: “Bear ye one another's burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ.”

points.hook: Baby, Mama's praying this one over you tonight, so just rest.
paragraphs: You don't have to figure it all out before you close your eyes. You don't have to solve tomorrow to deserve peace tonight. Lay it down — the job, the diagnosis, the child who won't call, the bill that's due — lay all of it at the foot of the bed like a worn-out coat, and let the God who never sleeps take the night shift so you don't have to. He's got it. Go to sleep.
points.verseText: “I will both lay me down in peace, and sleep: for thou, LORD, only makest me dwell in safety.”

cta.closingLine: If this spoke to you, let's stay connected.
